findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: When a caller invokes the returned disposer while the socket remains alive, later `message` events still invoke the supposedly detached handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also retain closures and multiply callback execution. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` in the cleanup callback.

findings.title: [P1] Restore message-listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
After any caller invokes the returned cleanup function, a subsequent `"message"` event still invokes the handler. This breaks cancellation/disposal, retains handlers indefinitely, and causes duplicate processing after repeated attach/cleanup cycles.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
Calling the disposer no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Any later message invokes a supposedly detached callback, and repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners and retained closures.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned teardown function no longer detaches the handler. If an EventEmitter-compatible socket remains live or is reused after teardown, untrusted messages still reach the stale handler, potentially after session/authorization revocation. Repeated attach/teardown cycles also retain handlers and amplify attacker-supplied messages, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
When callers invoke the returned disposer while the socket remains alive, the `"message"` listener stays registered. Repeated attach/dispose cycles therefore retain handlers and their captured memory indefinitely, while each message incurs increasing callback fan-out and CPU usage.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
